newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Police officer is first fatality in S.Korea riots.
newsitem.headline: Police officer is first fatality in S.Korea riots.

text.p: A South Korean riot policeman died after fierce clashes on Monday with militant students, the first fatality in four days of violent protests in Seoul to demand the resignation of President Kim Young-sam.
A police official said the 21-year-old officer, Yoo Ji-woong, died in hospital.
Witnesses said a number of police officers were beaten senseless as several thousand left-wing students armed with metal bars burst through a police cordon outside Hanyang University.
The students were trying to join a ceremony on the campus organised by an outlawed left-wing student body to inaugurate new office-holders.

The police official said bystanders summoned help from a passing driver for the officer as he lay dying. Doctors found he had a bloody nose and a bruise under one eye, but no other outward signs of serious injury.
Hand-to-hand fighting erupted on a bridge leading to the college after darkness fell.

Chanting students, some sporting white headbands reading "Kim Young-sam Resign", marched towards police blocking the bridge. They hurled crude petrol bombs and lashed out with iron bars at officers, who defended themselves with shields, clubs and volleys of teargas.

Earlier, state prosecutors vowed to crack down on the violence, orchestrated by the outlawed Hanchongryon body, which the government says takes orders from North Korea and is a threat to national security.

"We will deal sternly with any student violence. This violence is unacceptable. We will seek out any pro-communist students and punish them severely," said Shin Gun-soo, a senior prosecutor at the Seoul Prosecution Office.
The violence was sparked by Kim's refusal to bow to opposition demands and reveal how much he spent on his 1992 election campaign.
Allegations that Kim grossly overspent have surfaced in the final year of his presidency in the wake of a corruption scandal involving loans to the Hanbo Group.
A Seoul court on Monday sentenced Hanbo's 74-year-old patriarch to 15 years' jail after convicting him of bribing top aides to President Kim, bankers and others.
Chung Tae-soo was one of 10 people handed stiff prison sentences in a loans-for-kickbacks scandal involving Hanbo's failed steelmaking flagship.
The others are a former cabinet minister, three lawmakers with the ruling New Korea Party and one with the main opposition party, three ex-bankers and Chung's son, who is Hanbo's current chairman.
The Hanbo scandal has led to the arrest of Kim's second son and shattered the president's credibility.
At the height of Monday's fighting, one student ran screaming from police lines, flames pouring from the back of his shirt that had caught fire.

Injured officers were sprawled helplessly on the streets, their helmets scattered all around them. At one point, students disarmed and seized about 10 officers, but by late evening their fate was not clear.
A haze of teargas from shells fired by armoured police vehicles with multiple launchers engulfed the area. Students wore white cotton masks to protect themselves.
Towards midnight, around 10,000 students had gathered inside Hanyang University and fighting had ended.
